ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, a wooden board $B$ is placed on a horizontal ground, and a wooden block $A$ is placed on top of $B$. The right end of $A$ is fixed to a vertical wall by a horizontal light spring scale. A force $F=17\mathrm{N}$ is applied to pull $B$ to the left, causing it to move at a constant velocity. At this time, the reading of the spring scale remains constant at $F_{0}=8\mathrm{N}$. The masses of objects $A$ and $B$ are $m_{A}=4\mathrm{kg}$ and $m_{B}=5\mathrm{kg}$ respectively, and $g=10\mathrm{N/kg}$.

1. The coefficient of friction between $A$ and $B$.
2. The coefficient of friction between $B$ and the ground.

The right end of A is fixed to a vertical wall by a horizontal light spring scale. A force F = 17 N is applied to pull B to the left, causing it to move at a constant velocity. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, wooden board B is placed on a horizontal ground, and wooden block A is placed on the upper surface of B; the right side of A is connected to the vertical wall on the right through a horizontal spring dynamometer; the left end of wooden board B is subjected to a leftward pulling force F. A, B, F, and the spring are marked in the figure. Reasoning: B is pulled leftward and moves at a uniform speed, and the reading of the spring dynamometer is constantly F0 = 8 N, so A is balanced in the horizontal direction. The pulling force of the spring on A is to the right, with magnitude 8 N, so the sliding friction force of B on A is to the left, with magnitude also 8 N. The normal pressure between A and B is NA = mA g = 4 × 10 = 40 N, therefore μ_AB = f_AB / NA = 8 / 40 = 0.2. For wooden board B, perform force balance in the horizontal direction: the leftward pulling force F = 17 N; the friction force of A on B is to the right, with magnitude 8 N; the friction force of the ground on B is also to the right. Therefore the friction force of the ground on B is f_ground = 17 − 8 = 9 N. The supporting force of the ground on B bears the total gravity of A and B, N_ground = (mA + mB)g = (4 + 5) × 10 = 90 N. Therefore μ_B-ground = f_ground / N_ground = 9 / 90 = 0.1.
